Using the closed form I_α(X;Y) = (α/(α−1)) log ∫ (Σ_i p_i φ(y−√snr·x_i)^α)^{1/α} dy, I checked the high-SNR limit directly.

As snr → ∞ the Gaussian bumps around the points √snr·x_i separate, so near each bump a single term dominates. There (p_i φ^α)^{1/α} = p_i^{1/α} φ, and φ integrates to 1. The integral therefore tends to Σ_i p_i^{1/α}, and

lim I_α(X;Y) = (α/(α−1)) log Σ_i p_i^{1/α}.

The Rényi entropy of order β is H_β = (1/(1−β)) log Σ p_i^β. Setting β = 1/α gives 1/(1−1/α) = α/(α−1), which matches the limit exactly. So β = 1/α.

- Solution 1 claims β = α, which is wrong.
- Solution 2 gets β = 1/α. Its constant bookkeeping is more roundabout than needed, but the result is correct.
- Solution 3 claims β = 1/(1−α), which is wrong.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
